name: Berechiah
title: Zechariah's father and Levitical clan leader
summary: Berechiah was the son of Iddo and the father of the prophet Zechariah. He belonged to a Levitical clan and lived in the period after the Babylonian exile. His most significant role in the Bible is as a link in the genealogy of the prophet Zechariah, who played a central part in rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Zechariah's father
keyEvents.description: Berechiah is identified as the son of Iddo and the father of the prophet Zechariah in the introduction to the book of Zechariah.

keyEvents.title: Zechariah's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Berechiah is mentioned as a link in the prophetic lineage connecting Zechariah to his grandfather Iddo, a well-known priest and prophet.

keyEvents.title: The Genealogy in the Book of Ezra
keyEvents.description: In the book of Ezra, Zechariah is referred to as the son of Iddo, which may suggest that Berechiah died early and that Iddo was the most prominent ancestor. Nevertheless, Berechiah's role in the lineage is confirmed through the book of Zechariah.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: A Berechiah is mentioned among those who participated in rebuilding Jerusalem's wall, which may be linked to the same lineage and time period.

keyEvents.title: Jesus' reference to Zechariah's lineage
keyEvents.description: Jesus refers to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, who was killed between the temple and the altar, highlighting the significance of this lineage in biblical tradition.
